comment: JP2 0122: Suter's commentary, p. 90: chapter 33 continued: the size of the earth's shadow; the sixth and seventh columns of Tables 61-66 (primum and secundum dimidium rotae draconis); the rule behind them, with an example; the ratio of the shadow to the moon in Ptolemy, al-Battānī and al-Khwārizmī (notes 1-5).

observations: The page number «90» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01 continues the sentence that ends p. 89 (JP2 0121, L38), «dass die Methode der Berechnung der».

L01-L02, L18-L19, L34-L35: «Khaṇḍakhādyaka», in italics, with the dots under ṇ and ḍ and the macron, divided «Khaṇḍakhād-|yaka», «Khaṇ-|ḍakhādyaka», «Khaṇḍa-|khādyaka». L04: the headings of the sixth and seventh columns of Tables 61-66 in italics. L08: «Maslama al-Madjrīṭī» spaced.
L14, L21, L26, L31: «1 3/5», «2 3/5», the 3 raised and the 5 small on the line after a slash, written 1{sup:3}/{sub:5}. L22: «3sig.», the abbreviation raised: three signs.

L11-L29. Checked: 2′ 28″ × 5 = 12′ 20″; 32′ 56″ × 1 3/5 = 52′ 41.6″, «52′ 42″»; 52′ 47″ − 12′ 20″ = 40′ 27″. Per day the rule reads: the diameter of the shadow is (8 m − 25 s) : 60, m and s the daily true motions of the moon and the sun in minutes (twice the radius, 3 1/5 m : 24 − 10 s : 24). At 90° of anomaly the apparent radius of the moon in Table 63 is 15′ 58″ (p. 79, JP2 0111, L13-L14), and 40′ 27″ : 15′ 58″ = 2.53, within the 2.5 to 2.6 of L33. The values of the columns are to be compared with Tables 61-66.
The dashes: L03 and L11 «61—66», L28 «52′ 47″ — 12′ 20″» (the minus a long dash with a space on either side); the notes have the long dash of the small type.

Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Kh.», «Al-Bīrūnī», «Maslama al-Madjrīṭī», «Maslama», «Ptol.», «Batt.», «Brahmagupta», «Heiberg», «Manitius», «Nallino», «Burgess», «Thibaut»; italics: «Khaṇḍakhādyaka», the column headings, «buht», «Buht», «Beispiel :», «motus solis in hora», «Sūrya-Siddhānta», «Panchasiddhāntikā».
The colons and semicolons stand after the thin space of the edition (8-17 px measured).
